title: Wire an XOR network
prompt:
One unit cannot compute XOR. Two layers can. The starter has the wiring with every weight and bias set to 0. Change the numbers so that `xor(x1, x2)` gives 1 when exactly one input is 1, and 0 otherwise.

The test also reads your code: no `if`, no `^` and no `!=` inside `xor()`. Units only.
hints: Let hidden unit 1 count how many inputs are on. Weights 1 and 1, bias 0.
Let hidden unit 2 wake up only when both inputs are on. With ReLU, a bias of -1 does that.
The output takes h1 and subtracts something whenever h2 is awake. Try weight 1 on h1 and weight -2 on h2.
explain_after: A single perceptron cannot compute XOR because XOR is not linearly separable, and that is why layered networks matter [ml-084]. Your hidden layer uses ReLU, which outputs z when z is positive and 0 otherwise [ml-085]. These weights are hand-picked; a real network finds its own weights from examples.
